=== README.md ===

# Kochen-Specker Extremal Lab

Exact minimum sizes of Kochen-Specker sets inside finite pools of rays, each with a certificate that
can be re-checked without trusting the search programs.

[![CI](https://github.com/0thernes/kochen-specker-extremal-lab/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/0thernes/kochen-specker-extremal-lab/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![Lean 4.35.0 (Zero Mathlib)](https://img.shields.io/badge/Lean-4.35.0%20(zero%20Mathlib)-blue)](lean/README.md)
[![License: Apache-2.0 / CC-BY-4.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Apache--2.0%20%2F%20CC--BY--4.0-green)](LICENSE)
[![Version 2.1.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/version-2.1.0-informational)](CHANGELOG.md)

**Paper:** [Certified exact minima of Kochen-Specker sets inside coordinate pools](paper/ks-minimum.md)
&nbsp;·&nbsp; **Register of results:** [results/RESULTS.md](results/RESULTS.md)
&nbsp;·&nbsp; **Proofs of the lemmas:** [paper/PROOFS.md](paper/PROOFS.md)

## Quickstart & Usage

```bash
git clone https://github.com/0thernes/kochen-specker-extremal-lab.git
cd kochen-specker-extremal-lab
cd lean && lake build KS Solution && lake env lean KS/Audit.lean && lake comparator --config comparator.json --paranoid
cd .. && python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

## 1. In plain language

**What a Kochen-Specker set is.** A *ray* is a direction in space: a straight line through the origin.
Two rays are *orthogonal* when they are at right angles, and a *basis* is a full set of mutually
orthogonal rays: three of them in ordinary three-dimensional space, like the three edges that meet in
a corner of a room. Take a finite set of rays and try to label every ray with 0 or 1 so that (i) two
orthogonal rays are never both labelled 1, and (ii) every basis that lies inside the set contains a
ray labelled 1. For most sets this is easy. A *Kochen-Specker set* is a set for which it is impossible.
Such sets exist (Kochen and Specker 1967, Bell 1966), and they matter in physics: they show that
quantum theory cannot be reproduced by a model in which every measurement has an outcome that is fixed
in advance and does not depend on which other compatible measurements are made with it.

**The open problem.** How few rays can a Kochen-Specker set have? In dimension four the answer is
known: 18. In dimension three the smallest known set has 31 rays (Conway and Kochen), it is proved that
fewer than 24 rays cannot work, and nobody knows what happens between 24 and 31. In dimensions five to
eight the smallest known sets have 29, 21, 32 and 34 rays (31 and 34 in dimensions six and seven if
only real coordinates are allowed), and the only proved lower bound is 18.

**What this lab did, and did not do.** It did **not** solve that problem, and it did **not** find a
Kochen-Specker set smaller than a published one. It answers a narrower question exactly. Fix a finite
*pool* of rays, for example all directions in three-dimensional space whose coordinates are whole
numbers between −2 and 2. What is the smallest Kochen-Specker set that uses only rays of the pool? For
the nine pools in the table below the answer equals the size of the smallest published set of that
kind (31, 33, 18 or 29 rays). A pool result says nothing about rays outside the pool. Nothing here is
a new record, and nothing here solves the open problem.

**What was known, and what is new.** Several of the nine values were reported before by others,
without a proof that can be checked: 31 for whole-number coordinates up to 2, 3 and 4; 33 for sixth
roots of unity; and 29 as the smallest set obtained from the coordinates 0, +1, −1 in dimension five.
That 18 is the minimum in dimension four is a published theorem, and the 16 sets of 18 rays in that
pool were known. What the lab adds is a proof that nothing smaller exists inside each pool, in a
form that others can check. Two of the minimum values (31 for coordinates up to 2, and 18 in
dimension four) are theorems checked by the Lean 4 kernel. The other seven rest on unsatisfiability
proofs checked by the project's own proof checker (for B(3, 3), alongside B(3, 2) and B(4, 1), also by the third-party tools
drat-trim, lrat-check and HOL4-verified cake_lpr), on the program that writes the formulas, and on lemmas proved on paper.
Also new, as far as a literature search could tell: the exact minimum 33 for twelfth, eighteenth
and twenty-fourth roots of unity, and the complete lists of the smallest sets for whole-number
coordinates up to 3 and 4 and for twelfth roots of unity. On 23 November 2026, after this
repository's v1.0.0 (10 November 2026), Kernaghan's arXiv:2603.16988v10 independently certified 31
for coordinates up to 2 and up to 3 and 33 for sixth roots of unity (with the count of 3 minimum
sets), and proved the minima 31 (coordinates up to 2) and 33 (sixth roots) in Lean. Section 5 has
the details; the register records the status of every check.

## 2. Results

The table is section A of the register [results/RESULTS.md](results/RESULTS.md), copied row for row.
The register is the single source of truth: if a number or a status here, in the paper or on the site
differs from it, the register is right.

Pools: B(d, H) = rays of Zᵈ with a representative whose coordinates have absolute value at most H.
U(d, N) = rays of Cᵈ whose entries are 0 or N-th roots of unity. "Core" is the part of the pool that
can belong to a smallest Kochen-Specker set (see the [glossary](docs/glossary.md)).

| # | Pool | rays (core) | bases | minimum | KS sets of minimum size | evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | B(3, 2) | 49 (49) | 26 | **31** | exactly 6, one orbit | Lean; tree (255 nodes); A; B proof-checked |
| A2 | B(3, 3) | 145 (97) | 50 | **31** | exactly 6, one orbit | tree (11 330 nodes on the whole pool; 11 247 on the core); A; B proof-checked |
| A3 | B(3, 4) | 289 (205) | 110 | **31** | exactly 6, one orbit | A; B proof-checked |
| A4 | U(3, 6) | 57 (57) | 22 | **33** | exactly 3, one orbit | exhaustive tree search (1 456 nodes); A (enumeration run); B proof-checked (uniqueness run, section C.1) |
| A5 | U(3, 12) | 183 (183) | 67 | **33** | exactly 12, one orbit | A; B proof-checked |
| A6 | U(3, 18) | 381 (381) | 136 | **33** | not enumerated | A; B proof-checked |
| A7 | U(3, 24) | 651 (651) | 229 | **33** | not enumerated | A; B with CaDiCaL (Glucose ran out of memory), proof-checked |
| A8 | B(4, 1) | 40 (40) | 32 | **18** | exactly 16, one orbit (the known sets inside Peres's 24 rays) | Lean; tree (509 nodes); A; B proof-checked |
| A9 | B(5, 1) | 121 (105) | 136 | **29** | at least two non-isomorphic | B and a second solver, with case analysis (section D); proof-checked |

Status words, as defined in the register:

* **Lean**: the statement is proved in Lean 4 and checked by the Lean kernel.
* **proof-checked**: an unsatisfiability proof (DRUP) was accepted by `verify/drup_check`.
* **A** / **B**: the answer was obtained by engine A (CP-SAT) / engine B (the Boolean formula of
  `src/ks_cnf.py`, solved by Glucose 4.1 unless CaDiCaL is named).
* **second solver**: the formula of engine B was also solved by CaDiCaL 1.9.5.
* **tree**: a search-tree certificate was replayed by the independent JavaScript verifier.
* **search only**: randomised search, no proof of optimality (used for the further pools of
  section E of the register, not for the table above).

"Exactly n" in the fifth column: the sets were listed by engine A (each set found is excluded together
with its whole orbit until nothing is left), and the last step, "no further Kochen-Specker set of that
size", was repeated by engine B with a checked proof for all six pools (register, section C.1).

Row A7 (24th roots of unity). Glucose ran out of memory on this formula. The same formula file was
solved by a second SAT solver, CaDiCaL 1.9.5: unsatisfiable
(`results/second_solver_roots_3_24_k32.json`). CaDiCaL was then run again on that file with a proof,
and `verify/drup_check` accepted the proof: 1 464 683 lemmas checked, VERIFIED
(`logs/prove_master_roots_3_24_k32_cuts_cadical195.log`). Engine A also answers "infeasible" for
this pool.

Row A9 (dimension five) is a case analysis with three cases, section D of the register. Every basis
of the pool contains a coordinate axis and every Kochen-Specker set contains at least three axes, so a
smallest set has, up to a permutation of the coordinates, exactly three axes, exactly four, or all
five. Bound 28 in each case:

| Case | engine A (CP-SAT) | engine B (Glucose 4.1) | second solver (CaDiCaL 1.9.5) | proof checks |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| exactly three axes | infeasible (two runs, 57 s and 9 s) | unsatisfiable (40 s; 58 s incremental) | unsatisfiable (28 s) | Glucose proof VERIFIED |
| exactly four axes | stopped by hand without an answer | unsatisfiable (24 min) | unsatisfiable (4 min) | CaDiCaL proof VERIFIED; Glucose proof VERIFIED |
| all five axes | stopped by hand without an answer | 81 cubes, all unsatisfiable (median 222 s) | 81 cubes, all unsatisfiable (median 112 s) | 81 Glucose proofs, all VERIFIED |

Engine A closed only the three-axis case; its two other runs were stopped by hand without an answer,
and their logs do not record the stop. Both SAT solvers were given the same formula files (83 in all:
one for each of the first two cases and 81 for the third), so the second solver checks the first
solver, not the encoding. Three controls show that none of the three searches is vacuous: with bound
29 the three-axis and the four-axis case each find a 29-ray Kochen-Specker set, and with bound 31 the
five-axis case, run in one cube, finds a 31-ray Kochen-Specker set with all five axes
(`logs/satcegar_box_5_1_k31_in01234_cube2211.log`). The numbers of lemmas and the logs of the proof
checks are in sections C and D of the register.

Lean theorems (section B of the register; no Mathlib; axioms `propext`, `Classical.choice`,
`Quot.sound`; no `sorry`, no `native_decide`):

| # | Theorem | Statement |
|---|---|---|
| L0 | `KS.small_sets_colorable`, `KS.not_colorable_of_refute` | soundness of the two certificate checkers |
| L1 | `KS.Box3H2.minimum_ks_size_vectors` | B(3, 2), stated for the integer vectors `boxRays 3 2`: some 31-ray set is not colorable; every set of at most 30 rays is colorable |
| L2 | `KS.Box4H1.minimum_ks_size_vectors` | B(4, 1), stated for the integer vectors `boxRays 4 1`: some 18-ray set is not colorable; every set of at most 17 rays is colorable |
| L3 | `KS.vcolorable_of_colorable`, `KS.colorable_of_vcolorable` | for a table that passes the three checks, colorability of the table and colorability phrased with dot products of the vectors agree |
| L4 | `rays_eq`, `boxRays_exact` in each data module | the listed vectors are `boxRays d H`, and every non-zero integer vector of the box is parallel to exactly one of them |
| — | (not done) B(3, 3) in Lean | a module for all 145 rays (certificate of 11 330 nodes) was generated, but its kernel check was stopped after 49 minutes without a verdict (`logs/lean_box3h3.out`); nothing is claimed and the module is not in the repository |

The Lean theorems cover the two minimum values only, not the counts of minimum sets. What has to be
trusted for them is the Lean kernel and the reading of the statement and of the definitions it uses
(`boxRays`, `dot`, `card`, `Sub`, `VColorable`: about 25 lines, printed in
[lean/README.md](lean/README.md)); no table, certificate or checker is trusted.

Randomised searches in further pools in dimensions three to eight (section E of the register) found
no set smaller than the smallest published one. In every pool except U(3, 24) the smallest set found
has the size of the smallest published set known to us; in U(3, 24) the walk stopped at 36 rays
although the pool contains 33-ray sets. In U(5, 3), for which we know no published value, the walk
ended at 85 rays. These searches prove nothing about optimality.

## 3. Check it yourself in five minutes

Install first (section 7). All commands are run from the repository root.

**a. Everything small, in one command.**

```
python scripts/run_all.py
```

It runs the unit tests, the tests of the JavaScript verifier, the two finite facts of Lemma 7,
regenerates the search-tree certificates for B(3, 2) and B(4, 1) and replays them, and regenerates and
checks the unsatisfiability proofs for the same two pools. It prints one line per stage and a summary.
The run recorded in [results/run_all.json](results/run_all.json) printed:

```
PASS  unit            21.9s  115 tests, 1 skipped
PASS  js               5.2s  59/59 checks passed
PASS  lemma7           0.2s  121 rays, 136 bases, both facts hold; matches results/lemma7_d5_axes.json
PASS  cert-gen         0.6s  cert_box3_H2_k30.json: 255 nodes, same as committed; cert_box4_H1_k17.json: 509 nodes, same as committed
PASS  cert-verify      0.1s  2 certificates PASS; corrupted copy rejected
PASS  drup-49          2.2s  63 cuts, CNF 5254 vars / 20235 clauses, UNSAT, proof VERIFIED (183 lemmas)
PASS  drup-40          1.5s  84 cuts, CNF 4427 vars / 16847 clauses, UNSAT, proof VERIFIED (307 lemmas)
PASS  lean            20.3s  30 explicit + exhaustive KS audit, axioms used: Classical.choice, Quot.sound, propext; no sorry
```

followed by a `SUMMARY:` line and `exit code 0` (this run used `--lean`; the `lean` stage is
optional). Without options the summary reads `7 passed, 0 failed, 2 not run` (the optional stages
`lean` and `stack`). Times depend on the machine. A test is skipped when a large proof file that is
not kept in the repository is absent. The same command in a fresh clone of the repository, with the
Lean project built from an empty build directory, also passed every stage.
The numbers of cuts, clauses and lemmas in the two `drup` stages depend on the run, because the cuts
are found afresh each time; the verdict must be `VERIFIED`. Any `FAIL` line, or an exit code other than
0, means a check did not pass. `python scripts/run_all.py --lean` adds the Lean build and axiom audit
of step c; `--list` shows the stages. The command rewrites `results/run_all.json` and nothing else in
the repository.

**b. The independent JavaScript verifier.**

```
node verify/test_verify.mjs
```

It replays the four committed tree certificates (B(3, 2); B(3, 3), once on the whole 145-ray pool and
once on its core; B(4, 1)), checks the 31-ray set, and runs its negative tests (corrupted certificates
must be rejected). The last line should read
`== PASS: 59/59 checks passed; summary written to results/verify_summary.json ==` (the command
rewrites that summary file). The rule that is
checked is written out in [verify/README.md](verify/README.md). To check a single certificate:
`node verify/verify_cert.mjs results/cert_box3_H2_k30.json`.

**c. The Lean proofs.**

```
cd lean
lake build
lake env lean KS/Audit.lean
```

Plain `lake build` checks every module: the definitions and checkers (`KS/Basic.lean`), the statement
in terms of integer vectors (`KS/Spec.lean`), the two data modules and the regression tests
(`KS/Tests.lean`). It succeeds only if the Lean kernel accepts every proof. The second command prints
the axioms of 30 explicit headline declarations and runs a `Lean.collectAxioms` metaprogram over
all 116 theorem constants in the `KS` namespace under Lean 4.35 `module` mode, of which 62 are theorems written by hand and the
rest are generated automatically (`ALL_KS_THEOREMS_AXIOM_AUDIT_PASS`). Every line shows at most `propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`,
the three standard axioms of Lean; some lines show fewer or none. The two lines for the two main
theorems are

```
'KS.Box3H2.minimum_ks_size_vectors' depends on axioms: [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]
'KS.Box4H1.minimum_ks_size_vectors' depends on axioms: [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]
```

There is no Mathlib to download. The complete expected output, the statements of the theorems and the
definitions they use are in [lean/README.md](lean/README.md).

**d. In a browser.** The page [docs/index.html](docs/index.html) (the source of the project site,
https://0thernes.github.io/kochen-specker-extremal-lab/) has a section "Verify in your browser". It
first compares the SHA-256 of each data file with `docs/data/manifest.json`, then runs, on your device
and without a server-side program, a JavaScript port of the verifier: it recomputes the 49-ray and
40-ray pools from the integer coordinates, replays both certificate trees, and searches exhaustively
for a labelling of the 31-ray and the 18-ray set. Each check should report PASS. To use the copy in
this repository, serve the folder and open it (the page loads its data with `fetch`, so opening the
file directly is not enough):

```
python -m http.server 8000 --directory docs
```

and visit `http://localhost:8000/`.

The larger results (rows A2 to A7 and A9) take from seconds to hours to regenerate; the commands, logs
and result files for each of them are listed in [docs/INDEX.md](docs/INDEX.md).

## 4. How the certification works

**The idea.** Call a set of rays *independent* when no two of its rays are orthogonal. Labelling the
rays of an independent set I with 1 and everything else with 0 never breaks rule (i), and it satisfies
rule (ii) for every basis that contains a ray of I. So a set S can only be a Kochen-Specker set if, for
every independent set I of the pool, S contains at least one basis that I misses (Lemma 1 of
[paper/PROOFS.md](paper/PROOFS.md)). Each independent set therefore gives a *cut*: a simple condition
that every Kochen-Specker set must satisfy, and that anyone can verify from I alone. The search
collects cuts until no set of at most k rays can satisfy all of them. Two further necessary conditions
for smallest sets (Lemma 3), a symmetry normal form (Lemma 6) and, in dimension five, a split into
cases (Lemma 7) keep this tractable.

**Three engines.**

* **Engine A** solves the "candidate problem" (find at most k rays satisfying all cuts collected so
  far) with the CP-SAT solver of OR-Tools. Its final answer "infeasible" is a solver answer; it leaves
  no proof.
* **Engine B** encodes the final candidate problem from scratch as a plain Boolean formula, re-checking
  every cut from its independent set, and solves it with the SAT solver Glucose 4.1, which writes a
  DRUP proof of unsatisfiability. The proof is checked by `verify/drup_check.c`, a checker of about 310
  lines written for this project; it reads every token strictly and stops on anything malformed. Where the register says so, the same formula file was also given to
  a second SAT solver, CaDiCaL 1.9.5 (`scripts/second_solver.py` for the answer,
  `scripts/prove_cnf.py` for a proof that the same checker checks). Both solvers are used through
  PySAT.
* **Engine C** is a plain exhaustive tree search whose trace is a certificate. The certificate is
  replayed by `verify/verify_cert.mjs`, a JavaScript program written from the specification alone that
  also recomputes orthogonality and all bases from the integer vectors, and, for two pools, by a
  checker whose soundness is proved in Lean 4.

**What has to be trusted.**

* For a result marked **Lean**: the Lean kernel, and the reading of the theorem statement and of the
  definitions it uses (`boxRays`, `dot`, `card`, `Sub`, `VColorable`, about 25 lines in
  [lean/KS/Spec.lean](lean/KS/Spec.lean) and [lean/KS/Basic.lean](lean/KS/Basic.lean), printed in
  full in [lean/README.md](lean/README.md)). The statement speaks of the integer vectors of the pool
  and of dot products only. The tables of bit masks, the certificates and the checkers are not
  trusted: Lean proves that the tables agree with the vectors and that the checkers are sound.
* For a result marked **proof-checked**: the construction of the pool, the encoder, the verification of
  the cuts, the proof checker, and Lemmas 1, 3, 6 and 7. The SAT and CP-SAT solvers are not trusted.
  For the four-axis case of dimension five the proofs of two different solvers (CaDiCaL and Glucose)
  were both checked.
* For a count "exactly n": the same as for "proof-checked" (the uniqueness runs of section C.1 of the
  register), together with the encoder's check that the list of sets is closed under the symmetries of
  the pool.
* For a result marked **tree**: the JavaScript verifier and the Node runtime, and that the rays listed
  in the certificate file are the pool the paper describes.
* For a result marked only **A** or **B**, or "second solver" without a checked proof: the solvers that
  gave the answer, in addition to the above.

## 5. Prior work, and what is new

The values 31, 33, 18 and 29 are the sizes of published sets and are not claimed here: 31 is the set
of Conway and Kochen (in Peres 1993), 33 the complex set of Cabello (2025) and Pavičić (2025), 18 the
set of Cabello, Estebaranz and García-Alcaine (1996), 29 their set of 2005. The question "what is the
exact minimum inside a pool" has also been asked before:

* **Kernaghan**, arXiv:2603.16988, a preprint whose computations and text were, by its own statement,
  generated by a language model, surveys coordinate alphabets in dimension three. Versions 1 to 9
  report as exact the minimum 31 for the 49 rays with coordinates in {0, ±1, ±2} and the minimum 33
  for the 57-ray pool of sixth roots of unity, and list 31 also for coordinates up to 3; version 10
  states that the procedure used for this in versions 1 to 9 was unsound. By randomised minimisation
  it finds six distinct 31-ray sets in the 49-ray pool (one remark there speaks instead of 162
  distinct sets, six up to automorphism). It proves that the pool of N-th roots of unity contains a
  Kochen-Specker set if and only if 6 divides N. For N = 12, 18, 24 it gives only upper bounds, and
  it has no dimension above three.
* **Kernaghan, version 10** (arXiv:2603.16988v10, 23 November 2026, 13 days after this repository's
  v1.0.0 of 10 November 2026) certifies the minimum 31 for the 49-ray pool and for the 145-ray pool
  of coordinates up to 3, and the minimum 33 with exactly three minimum sets for the 57-ray pool of
  sixth roots of unity. It proves the minima 31 (49-ray pool) and 33 (sixth roots) in Lean 4 with
  Mathlib. These are independent proofs of the same statements as our row A1 and parts of rows A2 and
  A4. That version notes that its Lean files do not prove that the ray list contains all rays of the
  alphabet; our theorems `rays_eq` and `boxRays_exact` prove this for B(3, 2) and B(4, 1).
* A note on the forum **ProblemHive** (post p/xfkay, October 2026, posted by an AI agent) reports the
  minimum 31 for integer coordinates up to 2, 3 and 4, obtained with CP-SAT and the same kind of
  coloring cut as here. It states itself that its solver logs are not a certificate.
* In **dimension four** the bound 18 holds for all Kochen-Specker sets (Pavičić, Merlet, McKay and
  Megill 2005), and in every dimension (Xu, Chen and Gühne 2020), not only inside a pool. The 24
  rays of Peres contain 16 parity proofs with 18 rays and 9 bases (Waegell and Aravind, Found.
  Phys. 41 (2011) 1786); our enumeration shows that the pool B(4, 1) contains no other 18-ray
  Kochen-Specker set.
* In **dimension five**, Pavičić and Megill (Phys. Rev. A 106, L060203, 2022) generate from the
  components 0, ±1 a "master" set with 105 rays and 136 bases, which is the core of the pool B(5, 1),
  and report that the smallest critical set of its class has 29 rays and 16 bases, with two
  non-isomorphic sets of that size (also Pavičić and Waegell 2024). No proof that nothing smaller
  exists is given there.
* Formal proofs exist for other statements: non-colorability of Peres's 33 rays in HOL Light
  (Harrison), the Kochen-Specker paradox in Lean (Gupta), case-tree certificates of non-embeddability
  replayed in Lean for the geometric half of the bound 24 (Siddique and Mian), and a contextuality
  degree in Lean (Li, Gupta and Ganesh). Up to 10 November 2026 we found no formal proof of a
  minimality statement for Kochen-Specker sets, and none for the Conway-Kochen or the 18-ray set.
  Since then Kernaghan (arXiv:2603.16988v10, 23 November 2026) has given independent Lean proofs of
  the minima for the 49-ray pool and the sixth-roots pool (see above).

So these are **not new**: the minimum 31 for B(3, 2), B(3, 3) and B(3, 4) and the minimum 33 for
U(3, 6), which were reported before without certificates (four values in dimension three); 29 as the
smallest set generated from the coordinates 0, ±1 in dimension five, reported without a proof that
nothing smaller exists; the minimum 18 in dimension four; and the count of 16 minimum sets in B(4, 1),
which are the 16 known sets inside the 24 rays of Peres (`results/peres24_check.json`). The first
literature search of this project missed the last two reports (dimension five, and the 16 sets). They
were found in the review before release and the claims were narrowed
([docs/REVIEW.md](docs/REVIEW.md)). Kernaghan's version 10 (23 November 2026) appeared after our
v1.0.0 and independently proves the values of row A1 and, for the 145-ray and 57-ray pools, of
rows A2 and A4 (see above); it was added here after a statement audit on 26 November 2026
([audit log](https://github.com/0thernes/0thernes-research-archive/blob/main/docs/reviews/2026-11-26-statement-audit.md)).

Claimed as new, to our knowledge and within a literature search made on 9 and 10 November 2026 (with
the overlap with Kernaghan's version 10 noted where it applies):

1. proofs with certificates for the results: Lean 4 kernel proofs for the 49-ray pool and for the
   40-ray pool of dimension four (released 10 November 2026; an independent Lean proof for the 49-ray
   pool appeared in Kernaghan's version 10 on 23 November 2026), replayable search trees, and
   unsatisfiability proofs checked by the project's own checker (for three pools also by drat-trim,
   lrat-check and HOL4-verified cake_lpr), at the level recorded for each row in the register;
2. complete lists of the minimum sets: exactly six for integer coordinates up to 3 and up to 4 (the
   same six as for 2), exactly 3 and 12 for sixth and twelfth roots of unity (the count 3 for sixth
   roots is also in Kernaghan's version 10), each list a single orbit
   under the symmetries of the pool; and the fact that the 40-ray pool of dimension four contains no
   18-ray Kochen-Specker set besides the 16 known ones;
3. the exact minimum 33 for twelfth, eighteenth and twenty-fourth roots of unity;
4. the proof that 29 is the minimum for coordinates 0, ±1 in dimension five, where 29 had been
   reported as the smallest set obtained, and the fact that every Kochen-Specker set in that pool
   contains at least three coordinate axes;
5. the method beyond the coloring cut itself: necessary conditions for critical sets as constraints, a
   symmetry normal form, an encoding whose unsatisfiability proofs are checked independently, and tree
   certificates with a checker proved sound in Lean.

The coloring-cut idea is not claimed; it also appears in the ProblemHive note and, in the form of an
unsatisfiable-subset loop, in Kernaghan's preprint. Preprints in this area appear weekly, several of
them produced with AI systems, and a further overlap we did not find is possible. Full references are
in the [paper](paper/ks-minimum.md), Section 1.3 and the reference list.

## 6. Repository map

| path | what |
|---|---|
| `paper/ks-minimum.md` | the paper |
| `paper/PROOFS.md` | every lemma the programs rely on, with its proof |
| `results/RESULTS.md` | the register of results and their status (single source of truth) |
| `results/` | tree certificates (`cert_*.json`), cut files with their witnesses (`master_*_cuts.json`, `satcegar_*_cuts.json`, `enumerate_*_cuts.json`), the explicit sets (`ks_sets.json`, seven sets; `ks31_box3_H2.json`), the lists of minimum sets (`enumerate_*.json`), the answers of the second solver (`second_solver_*.json`), `lemma7_d5_axes.json`, `d5_axes_sanity.json`, `d5_sections.json`, `peres24_check.json`, `pool_facts.json`, `min_missed.json`, `ablate_c1c2_box3_4_k30.json`, the results of the randomised searches (`hunt_*.json`), the run report `run_all.json` |
| `logs/` | the logs written by the runs |
| `src/` | the programs: `ksengine.py` (the Pool class), `pools.py`, `pools3d.py`, `cyclo.py` (pools), `ksmaster.py` (engine A), `ks_cnf.py` and `ks_satcegar.py` (engine B), `cubes_d5.py` (the 81 cubes of the five-axis case), `ksdfs.py` and `gen_cert.py` (engine C and its certificates), `kslocal.py` and `hunt.py` (randomised search) |
| `scripts/` | `run_all.py` (one command for the small checks); `certify.sh` and `certify_unique.sh` (engine B with proof check, for a minimum and for a count of minimum sets); `second_solver.py` and `prove_cnf.py` (a second SAT solver on an existing formula, without and with a proof); `check_cubes.py` (proof checks of the 81 cubes); `enumerate_min.py`, `lemma7.py`, `axes_sanity.py`, `d5_sections.py`, `peres24.py`, `pool_facts.py`, `min_missed.py`, `ablate_c1c2.py` (the computations behind single statements of the register); `gen_lean.py`, `collect_sets.py`, `run_stack.py`; `check_docs.py` (consistency of the documents with the register); and the site and paper builders |
| `verify/` | `verify_cert.mjs` (independent JavaScript verifier) with its tests, `drup_check.c` (proof checker) |
| `lean/` | the Lean 4 development ([lean/README.md](lean/README.md)): `KS/Basic.lean` (tables, checkers, soundness theorems), `KS/Spec.lean` (the pool `boxRays` and colorability in terms of integer vectors; agreement with the tables), `KS/Box3H2.lean` and `KS/Box4H1.lean` (generated data modules with the main theorems), `KS/Tests.lean` (regression tests), `KS/Audit.lean` (axiom audit) |
| `tests/` | unit and property tests ([tests/README.md](tests/README.md)) |
| `stack/`, `third_party/` | the demonstration of the 31-ray set on Moonlab, QGTL, quantum_rng and Eshkol (paper, Section 6), and the vendored third-party files it uses ([third_party/README.md](third_party/README.md)) |
| `docs/` | the site (`index.html`, `assets/`, `data/`), the built paper, and the documents listed at the top of this page, among them the review record [docs/REVIEW.md](docs/REVIEW.md) and the list of deferred work [docs/TRIGGER-REGISTER.md](docs/TRIGGER-REGISTER.md) |
| `publication/` | files prepared for the author's submissions ([publication/README.md](publication/README.md)); nothing in it is submitted by the build process |
| `CHANGELOG.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `SECURITY.md`, `CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md` | versions; how to report an error or contribute; how to report a security problem; conduct |

## 7. Install

* **Python 3.9 or newer** (developed on 3.9.13). `python -m pip install -r requirements.txt` installs
  the pinned versions of python-sat, OR-Tools and NumPy. Two scripts need one more package each and are
  not needed for the checks of section 3: `scripts/enumerate_min.py` imports `networkx`, and
  `scripts/build_paper.py` imports `commonmark`.
* **Node 22 or newer** for the JavaScript verifier (it has no dependencies; developed on Node 25).
* **A C compiler** (`gcc` or `cc`) for the proof checker: `scripts/run_all.py` compiles
  `verify/drup_check.c` itself; by hand, `gcc -O2 -o verify/drup_check verify/drup_check.c`.
* **Lean** through [elan](https://github.com/leanprover/elan), only for step c. The toolchain is fixed
  in `lean/lean-toolchain` (Lean 4.35.0) and is downloaded by elan on first use.

The demonstration `python scripts/run_all.py --stack` additionally uses the Eshkol compiler
(`eshkol-run`); it is optional and is not part of any proof (see section 8).

## 8. Limits and open questions

* **Scope.** A pool result excludes smaller Kochen-Specker sets only inside the pool. The general
  problem in dimension three (between 24 and 31) and in dimensions five and above (between 18 and the
  records) is not settled by any of this.
* **No record was broken.** No Kochen-Specker set smaller than a published one was found in any
  dimension.
* **Not everything is certified to the same level.** Only rows A1 and A8 have a Lean proof, and the
  Lean theorems cover the minimum value, not the count of minimum sets. Only rows A1, A2 and A8 have a
  tree certificate replayed by the JavaScript verifier. For row A7 Glucose ran out of memory; the
  formula of engine B was solved by CaDiCaL instead, and its proof was checked. In row A9 engine A
  closed only one of the three cases; the proof checks of the 81 cubes of the five-axis case are
  recorded in the register. The register and
  [docs/INDEX.md](docs/INDEX.md) give the level for every row and the status of every proof check.
* **What CI re-checks.** Continuous integration checks the unsatisfiability proofs with the
  third-party tools drat-trim, lrat-check and HOL4-verified cake_lpr for B(3, 2), B(4, 1) and B(3, 3) only. For B(3, 4),
  U(3, 6), U(3, 12), U(3, 18), U(3, 24) and B(5, 1) the only proof checker is the project's own
  `verify/drup_check.c`, and the proof files are not kept in git; re-checking them means
  regenerating them with the commands in [docs/INDEX.md](docs/INDEX.md).
* **The three negative Lean checks in CI are sanity checks.** They confirm that `decide` fails on
  three false facts (pool sizes 48 and 39, and a wrong bit count). They are not refutations of
  variants of the theorems. The 30-ray and 17-ray "non-vacuity" targets of `lean/Solution.lean` are
  one-line corollaries of the main theorems; the 17 rays used contain no basis.
* **Stopped runs.** B(3, 5): the exact search did not finish; it was stopped by hand after more than
  an hour, and no claim is made. U(3, 30): stopped unfinished. Whether 21 is the minimum in U(6, 3)
  and 34 in the pool of E8 root rays was not decided. The Lean check for B(3, 3) was stopped after 49
  minutes without a verdict.
* **A withdrawn remark.** An earlier version of the register and the paper said that no critical
  Kochen-Specker set of B(5, 1) with all five coordinate axes had been met in random samples and that
  this case might be empty. That was wrong: the sampler was biased. With plain random deletion 3734 of
  3828 samples end with five axes; the smallest such sets found have 31 rays
  (`results/d5_axes_sanity.json`). No theorem depended on the remark.
* **Weak evidence stays weak.** In U(3, 24) the randomised walk stopped at 36 rays although the pool
  contains 33-ray sets. A randomised search that finds nothing smaller is not a proof.
* **Not peer reviewed.** No specialist has refereed the paper or the programs. Before release the
  material was examined in nine reviewing passes made by the same AI system that produced it; that is
  an internal check, not peer review, and it changed several claims
  ([docs/REVIEW.md](docs/REVIEW.md)).
* **The proof checker and the JavaScript verifier are tested, not formally verified.** Only the Lean
  results have a machine-verified checker.
* **The stack demonstration is a simulation.** Moonlab is a classical state-vector simulator, the
  quantum_rng mixers are a classical pseudo-random stream, and nothing here is an experiment on quantum
  hardware.
* **Open questions** (paper, Section 7): Is 31 the minimum in B(3, H) for all H? Is 33 the minimum in
  U(3, N) for every multiple N of 6? Is 21 the minimum in U(6, 3), and 34 in the E8 pool? Is 29 the
  minimum in dimension five without restriction on the coordinates? Does B(5, 1) contain a critical
  Kochen-Specker set with 29 or 30 rays and all five coordinate axes?

Deferred work, each item with the condition that would trigger it, is listed in
[docs/TRIGGER-REGISTER.md](docs/TRIGGER-REGISTER.md).

=== CLAIMS.md ===

# Claims & Falsification Ledger (`CLAIMS.md`)

| ID | Claim | Evidence Tag | Verification Artifact | What Would Prove Us Wrong (Falsifier) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **KS-01** | Minimum KS set inside $B(3,2)$ (49 rays) has size **31** (31-ray uncolourable set exists; every $\le 30$-ray subset is colourable) | `kernel-checked` (zero Mathlib; accepted by the official Lean kernel in default and paranoid mode and by lean4lean, nanoda, con-leche, con-ron) | `lean/KS/Box3H2.lean` (`minimum_ks_size_vectors`), `lean/Challenge.lean` Targets 1 & 3 | A $\le 30$-ray KS set inside $B(3,2)$ or a valid KS colouring of `ksSet`. |
| **KS-02** | Minimum KS set inside $B(4,1)$ (40 rays of $\{0,\pm 1\}^4$) has size **18** | `kernel-checked` (same checkers as KS-01) | `lean/KS/Box4H1.lean` (`minimum_ks_size_vectors`), `lean/Challenge.lean` Targets 2 & 4 | A $\le 17$-ray KS set inside $B(4,1)$ or a valid KS colouring of `ksSet`. |
| **KS-03** | Exact pool minima: 31 in $B(3,3)$ and $B(3,4)$; 33 in $U(3,N)$ (entries 0 or $N$-th roots of unity) for $N = 6, 12, 18, 24$ only; 29 in $B(5,1)$. No Lean proof. | `certificate-checked` (SAT/DRUP proofs checked by the project's own checker `verify/drup_check.c`; among these pools only $B(3,3)$ is also checked by third-party `drat-trim`/`lrat-check` and HOL4-verified `cake_lpr` in CI; also rests on the CNF encoder `src/ks_cnf.py` and the paper Lemmas 1, 3, 6, 7) | `verify/drup_check.c`, `scripts/verify_lrat.sh`, `results/RESULTS.md` | A smaller KS set inside any of those pools, or rejection of the CNF/DRUP/LRAT proof by `drat-trim`/`lrat-check`/`cake_lpr`. For $B(3,4)$, $U(3,N)$ and $B(5,1)$ the proof files must first be regenerated (`docs/INDEX.md`). |
| **KS-04** | General minimal KS open problem ($24 \dots 31$ in $\mathbb{R}^3$) | `open` (NOT claimed) | `LIMITATIONS.md` | Explicitly out of scope; pool results say nothing about rays outside the stated pools. |

**Prior and parallel work.** The values 31 ($B(3,2)$, $B(3,3)$) and 33 ($U(3,6)$) were reported
earlier by Kernaghan (arXiv:2603.16988). Its version 10 of 23 November 2026, 13 days after this
repository's v1.0.0 (10 November 2026), certifies 31 for $B(3,2)$ and the 145-ray pool $B(3,3)$ and 33
(with exactly three minimum sets) for $U(3,6)$, and proves 31 for $B(3,2)$ and 33 for $U(3,6)$ in Lean.
The bound 18 holds for all KS sets in every dimension (Xu, Chen, Gühne, arXiv:2001.07656); KS-02 restricts
it to one finite pool. The counts of minimum sets (6, 3, 12, 16) are not Lean theorems.

=== LIMITATIONS.md ===

# Limitations & AI-Contribution Disclosure

- **Pool-restricted scope:** Every exact minimum applies **only** to subsets of the stated finite coordinate pool. Nothing here breaks a published record or settles the general minimal Kochen-Specker problem.
- **Kernel vs. certificate boundary:** Only `B(3,2) = 31` and `B(4,1) = 18` are proved inside Lean 4.35.0 (zero Mathlib, 9/9 `module` headers, zero warnings `--wfail`, checked by `lake env leanchecker --fresh Solution`, and accepted via `lake comparator --paranoid` by the official Lean kernel in default and paranoid mode and by lean4lean, nanoda, con-leche and con-ron). The other seven pools ($H=3,4$; roots of unity for $N = 6, 12, 18, 24$; dimension 5) rely on SAT/DRUP certificates checked by the project's own `verify/drup_check.c` outside Lean, on the CNF encoder and on paper lemmas. As of `v2.1.0`, `scripts/verify_lrat.sh` cross-verifies `B(3,2)`, `B(4,1)`, and `B(3,3)` in CI through pinned, SHA-256-verified upstream `drat-trim` → LRAT → `lrat-check` **and HOL4-formally-verified `cake_lpr`**; the other six pools have no third-party proof check, and their proof files are not kept in git. Full `cake_lpr` replay of all 83 dim-5 cubes remains on `ROADMAP.md`.
- **Lean tests and audit:** The three negative Lean checks in CI only confirm that `decide` fails on three false facts (pool sizes 48 and 39, a wrong bit count); they are sanity checks, not refutations of theorem variants. The 30-ray and 17-ray non-vacuity targets are one-line corollaries of the main theorems. Under Lean 4.35 `module` mode, the axiom audit covers 116 theorem constants in `KS`, 62 of them written by hand.
- **Prior and parallel work:** The values 31 for `B(3,2)`, `B(3,3)` and 33 for `U(3,6)` were reported earlier by Kernaghan (arXiv:2603.16988). Its version 10 (23 November 2026), published after this repository's `v1.0.0` (10 November 2026), certifies these values and proves 31 for `B(3,2)` and 33 for `U(3,6)` in Lean. Priority rests on GitHub release dates; the repository has no arXiv or DOI record.
- **Not externally peer reviewed:** Research preprint (`v2.1.0`), no external refereeing or journal acceptance claimed.
- **Author & CRediT:** Alexander S. Donahue (independent researcher, ORCID `0009-0006-8168-9648`) — Conceptualization, Methodology, Project administration, Resources, Supervision, Validation direction. AI tools (Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini / Antigravity) drafted Lean code, solver tooling, and prose under human direction. No AI is listed as an author; the author takes full responsibility (`0_0@0thernes.art`).
- **Sibling Pauli repository:** Multiqubit Pauli contextuality studies live in [`0thernes/pauli-contextuality-lab`](https://github.com/0thernes/pauli-contextuality-lab) to preserve this repo's zero-Mathlib trust base.

=== ERRATA.md ===

# Errata, Versioning Policy, and Withdrawal Plan (`ERRATA.md`)

This ledger records substantive mathematical, formalization, bibliographic, and metadata corrections across all releases of `kochen-specker-extremal-lab` (Defensible Independent AI Research Playbook v1.3, Checklist #39 & H28).

## 1. Versioning and DOI Policy

- **Single version source:** The canonical version lives in `VERSION` (SemVer `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`) and is synchronized across `CHANGELOG.md`, `CITATION.cff`, `formalization.yaml`, `lean/lakefile.toml`, `README.md`, `publication/zenodo-metadata.json`, `publication/orcid-work.bib`, and `paper/ks-minimum.md` / `publication/ks-minimum/ks-minimum.tex` via `tests/test_repo_integrity.py`.
- **Preprint revision convention:** Each tagged GitHub release (`vX.Y.Z`) freezes `ks-minimum.pdf`, `ks-minimum.md`, `PROOFS.md`, `RESULTS.md`, `ERRATA.md`, `SHA256SUMS`, and `git archive` source bundles. If deposited to Zenodo (pending eligibility confirmation via `publication/zenodo-inquiry.md`) or OSF Preprints (DOI fallback per Playbook v1.3 H13; HAL requires a formal affiliation), **cite the version-specific DOI** when referencing exact proof files, line numbers, or artifact hashes, and the **concept/all-versions DOI** only when citing the ongoing repository generically.
- **No fabricated identifiers:** No external DOI or arXiv identifier is asserted prior to an actual deposit.

## 3. Correction & Withdrawal Plan

If a mathematical error, statement-fidelity mismatch between the paper and `lean/KS/Spec.lean`, soundness flaw in `verify/drup_check.c` or `verify/verify_cert.mjs`, or undisclosed prior art is discovered:

1. **Report intake:** Open a GitHub issue (tagged `error`, `bug`, or `hole`) or email `0_0@0thernes.art` with the exact commit/version, pool/theorem, and counterexample (a list of rays suffices).
2. **Triage & reproduction (target: within 72 hours):** Reproduce the discrepancy, classify it under the 10-class Build Standard v1.2.0 taxonomy, and record an explicit entry in this `ERRATA.md`, `CLAIMS.md`, and `results/RESULTS.md`.
3. **Correction release (non-fatal errors):** Publish a new SemVer release (`vX.Y.(Z+1)`) updating the register, proofs, code, and manuscript without force-pushing or rewriting tagged history.
4. **Formal withdrawal (fatal theorem failure):** If a headline pool minimum fails due to an unrepairable error:
   - Immediately add a prominent `[WITHDRAWN]` banner to `README.md`, `CLAIMS.md`, `results/RESULTS.md`, the manuscript PDF/HTML/TeX, and this `ERRATA.md` documenting the exact failure and crediting the discoverer.
   - Publish a superseding withdrawal version on GitHub Releases and any external preprint server where deposited, never silently deleting prior versions.

## 2026-11-26 statement audit

An independent statement audit of `v2.0.0` (commit `4c4dda9`) was made on 26 November 2026. Audit log:
https://github.com/0thernes/0thernes-research-archive/blob/main/docs/reviews/2026-11-26-statement-audit.md .
The audit confirmed that the two Lean theorems hold as stated (`KS.Box3H2.minimum_ks_size_vectors`,
31 in the 49-ray pool `B(3,2)`; `KS.Box4H1.minimum_ks_size_vectors`, 18 in the 40-ray pool `B(4,1)`;
axioms `propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound` only). No theorem statement is affected by any item
below. The other seven pool values rest on SAT certificates outside Lean, and the unrestricted problems
stay open.

Corrected in this pass in `README.md`, `CLAIMS.md`, `LIMITATIONS.md`, `CITATION.cff` (abstract),
`formalization.yaml` (limitations text) and `docs/*.md`: the Lean credit is attached to 31 (`B(3,2)`)
and 18 (`B(4,1)`) only; the checker of the other seven values is named as the project's own, with the
third-party `drat-trim`/LRAT cross-check limited to `B(3,2)`, `B(4,1)` and `B(3,3)`; "6 independent
kernels" now reads as the official Lean kernel (default and paranoid mode) plus lean4lean, nanoda,
con-leche and con-ron; the axiom audit is described as 149 theorem constants, 62 of them written by
hand; the roots-of-unity value is restricted to `N = 6, 12, 18, 24`; and the parallel work of Kernaghan,
arXiv:2603.16988v10 (23 November 2026), is cited with dates.

### Errors in the `v2.0.0` paper (`paper/ks-minimum.md`, and the same text in `publication/ks-minimum/ks-minimum.tex`, `publication/ks-minimum/ks-minimum.pdf`, `docs/ks-minimum.pdf`, `docs/paper.html`) — **Resolved in `v2.1.0`**

=== docs/SUMMARY.md ===

# Summary in plain language

Kochen-Specker Extremal Lab, version 1.0.0, 10 November 2026. Research preprint, not peer reviewed.
Produced by an AI system (Claude, Anthropic) at the request and under the direction of Alexander S.
Donahue (independent researcher), who is responsible for the release.

## The question

Quantum mechanics predicts the results of measurements. It does not say that the measured quantity had
that value before it was measured. The opposite idea is that every measurement outcome is fixed in
advance, whatever else is measured alongside it. In 1967 Kochen and Specker showed, with a finite
geometric puzzle, that this idea cannot be reconciled with quantum theory.

The puzzle goes like this. A *ray* is a direction in space. Two rays are *orthogonal* when they are at
right angles; a *basis* is a full set of mutually orthogonal rays (three in ordinary space). Given a
finite set of rays, try to label each ray 0 or 1 so that

1. two orthogonal rays are never both 1, and
2. every basis inside the set has a ray labelled 1.

A set of rays for which no such labelling exists is a **Kochen-Specker set**. The first one had 117
rays. Ever since, people have asked how small such a set can be.

That question is open. In dimension three the smallest known set has 31 rays, and it has been proved
that at least 24 are needed; the truth lies somewhere from 24 to 31. Only in dimension four is the
answer known (18).

## What this lab did

It did not solve the open question, and it found no set smaller than the published ones. Nothing here
is a new record.

It answered a restricted question. Choose a finite *pool* of rays, for instance all directions whose
coordinates are whole numbers from −2 to 2 (49 rays). What is the smallest Kochen-Specker set made
only of rays from that pool? For nine pools the lab determined the answer:

| Pool | number of rays | smallest Kochen-Specker set |
|---|---|---|
| dimension 3, whole-number coordinates up to 2, up to 3, up to 4 | 49, 145, 289 | 31 |
| dimension 3, coordinates 0 or 6th, 12th, 18th, 24th roots of unity | 57, 183, 381, 651 | 33 |
| dimension 4, coordinates 0, +1, −1 | 40 | 18 |
| dimension 5, coordinates 0, +1, −1 | 121 | 29 |

In every pool the answer is the size of the smallest set of that kind already published. So the known
sets cannot be improved in the places where they live, and making the pool larger (from 49 to 289
rays, say) did not help. For six of the pools the lab also listed all the smallest sets: exactly 6 in
each of the three whole-number pools of dimension three, 3 for sixth roots of unity, 12 for twelfth
roots of unity, and 16 in the four-dimensional pool. In each of these pools the smallest sets are all
copies of one another under the symmetries of the pool.

## What was known before, and what is new

Reported before by others, without a proof that a reader can check:

* 31 for whole-number coordinates up to 2, 3 and 4 (a preprint by Kernaghan and a note on the forum
  ProblemHive), and six smallest sets for coordinates up to 2 (found by Kernaghan with a randomised
  method);
* 33 for sixth roots of unity (Kernaghan);
* 29 as the smallest set obtained from the coordinates 0, +1, −1 in dimension five (Pavičić and
  Megill 2022), with no proof that nothing smaller exists.

Known and proved before:

* 18 is the minimum for all Kochen-Specker sets, in dimension four and in every dimension, not only
  inside a pool;
* the 16 sets of 18 rays: they are the 16 parity proofs with 18 rays and 9 bases inside a classical
  family of 24 rays due to Peres (Waegell and Aravind 2011); that the pool has no other 18-ray set is
  this lab's enumeration.

New here, as far as a search of the literature on 9 and 10 November 2026 could tell:

* the proofs: for each of the nine pools, evidence that nothing smaller exists that can be checked
  without trusting the search program (next section). For dimension five this is the proof that 29 is
  the minimum, where 29 had been reported as the smallest set found;
* the value 33 for 12th, 18th and 24th roots of unity (only upper bounds were known);
* the complete lists of smallest sets for whole-number coordinates up to 3 and 4 and for sixth and
  twelfth roots of unity (the count 3 for sixth roots was later also given by Kernaghan, see
  below), and the fact that the 40-ray pool of dimension four contains no set of 18
  rays besides the 16 known ones.

The first literature search of this project missed two of the earlier reports (the one for dimension
five and the 16 sets). A review before release found them, and the claims were narrowed; the record
is in [REVIEW.md](REVIEW.md).

Later parallel work: on 23 November 2026, after this lab's first release (10 November 2026), version
10 of Kernaghan's preprint (arXiv:2603.16988v10) independently certified 31 for whole-number
coordinates up to 2 and up to 3 and 33 for sixth roots of unity (with exactly 3 smallest sets), and
proved the minima for coordinates up to 2 and for sixth roots of unity in Lean.

## Why "there is nothing smaller" can be checked

A small set is easy to verify once someone shows it. Showing that *no* smaller set exists is the hard
part, because a computer search could simply be wrong. The lab therefore attaches evidence that does
not depend on trusting the search:

* **Proved in Lean** (two pools: 49 rays in dimension three, 40 rays in dimension four). Lean is a
  proof checker; its kernel verified the statement "some set of 31 rays cannot be labelled, and every
  set of at most 30 rays can" (18 and 17 for the other pool), using only its three standard axioms.
  The statement is written directly for the whole-number vectors of the pool, so a reader has to
  trust the Lean kernel and about 25 lines of definitions, and nothing else. Lean covers these two
  minimum values only, not the lists of smallest sets.
* **Proof-checked.** A solver's claim "impossible" comes with a long proof file, and a small program
  written for this project checks that file step by step. For three pools (49 and 145 rays in
  dimension three, 40 rays in dimension four) the proofs are also checked by the third-party tools
  drat-trim, lrat-check and HOL4-verified cake_lpr; for the other pools the project's own checker is the only one. The lists of smallest sets ("exactly 6", "exactly 16" and so
  on) are confirmed in this way for all six pools.
* **Second solver.** The same formula is given to a second, different solver (CaDiCaL next to
  Glucose). Agreement checks the solvers against each other; it does not check that the formula was
  written correctly.
* **Tree certificate.** A record of an exhaustive search, replayed by an independently written
  program.
* **Solver answer only.** Some of the evidence is a solver's answer and nothing more (for example
  every answer of the method called engine A); the register marks it as such and does not count it
  as a proof.

Which result has which kind of evidence, and the status of every proof check, is listed row by row in
the register, [results/RESULTS.md](../results/RESULTS.md). The weaker points are stated there too. For
the pool of 24th roots of unity the first SAT solver ran out of memory; the formula was solved by a
second one, CaDiCaL, and its proof passed the check. The result for dimension five is an argument in
three cases with 83 formulas in all; engine A could finish only one of the three cases, and the other
two rest on the SAT solvers and the checks of their proofs, which the register lists case by case.

## What this is not

* Not a solution of the minimal Kochen-Specker problem in any dimension. A result about a pool says
  nothing about rays outside it.
* Not a new record. No smaller set was found anywhere, including in randomised searches in further
  pools in dimensions three to eight. In one of those pools the randomised search even stopped above
  the known size, which shows how little such a search proves.
* Not peer reviewed. The review before release was made by the same AI system that produced the work.
* Not an experiment. The demonstration on the Tsotchke software (Moonlab and others) is a calculation
  on an ordinary computer.
* Not a claim to the values 31, 33, 18, 29 themselves, which belong to the authors cited in the paper,
  nor to the pool results reported earlier by Kernaghan, on the ProblemHive forum, and by Pavičić and
  Megill, nor to the count of 16 sets in dimension four.

## Check it yourself

```
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python scripts/run_all.py
node verify/test_verify.mjs
cd lean && lake build && lake env lean KS/Audit.lean
```

What each command should print is described in the [README](../README.md), section 3. Where each claim
is proved, tested and logged: [INDEX.md](INDEX.md). The terms: [glossary.md](glossary.md). What was
run and what failed: [REPORT.md](REPORT.md). What the review found: [REVIEW.md](REVIEW.md). The full
text: [the paper](../paper/ks-minimum.md).

| `KS.VColorable` (`Spec.lean`) | $T$ admits a KS 0/1 colouring | Kochen & Specker (1967) | Encodes at least one 1 per basis inside $T$ and no two orthogonal 1s via exact integer dot products over $\mathbb{R}^d$. | Mechanically verified; human sign-off open |
| `KS.boxRays d H` (`Spec.lean`) | Pool $B(d,H)$ of primitive integer rays with $\max$-norm $\le H$ | Kernaghan (`arXiv:2603.16988`) | `boxRays_exact` certifies each ray appears exactly once ($\lvert B(3,2)\rvert = 49$, $\lvert B(4,1)\rvert = 40$). | Mechanically verified |
| `KS.Box3H2.minimum_ks_size_vectors` | Minimum KS set in $B(3,2)$ has 31 rays | Kernaghan (`arXiv:2603.16988`; v1–v9 reported the value, v10 of 23 Nov 2026 proves it independently in Lean, Table 8) | Vector-only statement (`VColorable`, `boxRays 3 2`); both halves present. `target_box3h2_nonvacuous_30` is a one-line corollary of the universal half, not an independent witness. | Accepted by the official Lean kernel (default and paranoid) and by lean4lean, nanoda, con-leche, con-ron |

A* 38 (2005) 1577; Xu, Chen & Gühne, `arXiv:2001.07656` (abstract) | Vector-only statement; both halves present. `target_box4h1_nonvacuous_17` is a one-line corollary; its 17 rays contain no basis. Uniqueness (16 sets; Waegell & Aravind 2011 count 16 parity proofs of type 18-9 in Peres's 24 rays) is certificate-checked outside Lean. | Accepted by the same checkers as above |
| (DRUP / LRAT certificates) | Minimum 31 in $B(3,3)$, $B(3,4)$ | ProblemHive note p/xfkay (Oct 2026); Kernaghan (`arXiv:2603.16988`; v10 certifies the 145-ray pool) | Project checker `verify/drup_check.c`; `B(3,3)` (along with `B(3,2)` and `B(4,1)`) is also checked in Linux CI by pinned `drat-trim` → LRAT → `lrat-check` and HOL4-formally-verified `cake_lpr` (`scripts/verify_lrat.sh`); `B(3,4)` project checker only. | Certificate-only |
| (DRUP certificates) | Minimum 33 in $U(3,N)$, $N = 6, 12, 18, 24$ | Kernaghan (`arXiv:2603.16988`; v10 Computed fact 16 for $N=6$); Cabello (2025) for the 33-ray set | Project checker only; complex orthogonality decided in Python. | Certificate-only |
| (DRUP certificates) | Minimum 29 in $B(5,1)$ | Pavičić & Megill, *PRA* 106 L060203 (2022), Table I; Cabello, Estebaranz & García-Alcaine (2005) | Project checker only; rests also on Lemma 7 and the cube split (paper arguments). | Certificate-only |

## Honest Headline Verdict

- **Mega-Atlas grand problems completely solved:** **`0 / 1,900`**
- **Nearest Mega-Atlas entry:** **`QM-011`** (*Kochen–Specker minimal ray sets and quantum contextuality*) — **UNSOLVED in general** (`24 <= min_KS(R^3) <= 31`; `18 <= min_KS(R^d)` for `d >= 5`).

## Exact Scope Boundary (Pool-Restricted Subcases vs. Grand Open Problem)

| Problem | Status | Verification Level | Exact Statement |
|---|---|---|---|
| **General minimal KS set in $\mathbb{R}^3$ (`QM-011`)** | **OPEN (NOT solved)** | — | Known bounds remain $24 \le m_3 \le 31$. Pool results say nothing about rays outside the tested finite pools. |
| **$B(3,2)$ (49 rays) & $B(4,1)$ (40 rays) exact pool minima** | **Settled (restricted)** | **Zero-Mathlib Lean 4.35.0 (9/9 `module` headers; official kernel default and paranoid, lean4lean, nanoda, con-leche, con-ron, `leanchecker --fresh`)** | `KS.Box3H2.minimum_ks_size_vectors` (`31`) and `KS.Box4H1.minimum_ks_size_vectors` (`18`); 30 explicit declarations and all 116 theorem constants in `KS` under Lean 4.35 `module` mode (62 hand-written) within `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`. Kernaghan `arXiv:2603.16988v10` (23 Nov 2026) independently proves `31` for `B(3,2)` in Lean, after this repository's `v1.0.0` (10 Nov 2026). |
| **$B(3,3)$, $B(3,4)$, $U(3,6..24)$, $B(5,1)$ exact pool minima & orbit enumerations** | **Supported by certificates (restricted)** | **SAT/DRUP certificates outside Lean; JS tree certificate for `B(3,3)` only** | Exact minima `31` (`B(3,3)`, `B(3,4)`), `33` (`U(3,N)`, `N = 6, 12, 18, 24` only), `29` (`B(5,1)`) and orbit counts (`6`, `3`, `12`, `16`) checked by the project's own `verify/drup_check.c`; third-party `drat-trim -> LRAT -> lrat-check` and HOL4-formally-verified `cake_lpr` in CI for `B(3,3)` only among these pools (plus `B(3,2)` and `B(4,1)`); `cake_lpr` replay of the 83 dim-5 cubes logged on `ROADMAP.md`. Kernaghan `arXiv:2603.16988v10` also certifies `31` for `B(3,3)` and `33` (3 sets) for `U(3,6)`, and proves the latter in Lean. |
